title: Effects express architectural dependencies

nodes.summary: Layered effectful architecture; only native plumbing interpreters touch IO
nodes.detail: Host operations use effectful with explicit rows, separated into domain, porcelain capabilities, porcelain interpreters, plumbing capabilities with native interpreters, and adapters/composition. Only native plumbing interpreters may use IOE or native libraries, and GHC package visibility plus import checks enforce the dependency DAG.

realised.evidence: Domain/plumbing packages and check-imports.mjs from PR #6; first plumbing-interpreters package with IO-confined ProcessExecution in PR #7

nodes.summary: Capability and Interpreter module namespaces for porcelain and plumbing
nodes.detail: Modules live under Kyyn.{Porcelain,Plumbing}.{Capability,Interpreter}.*; a capability owns its vocabulary and combinators, its interpreter owns handler installation, and no .IO suffix is used until a second interpreter exists.

realised.evidence: Kyyn.Plumbing.Capability.FileSystem / Kyyn.Plumbing.Interpreter.FileSystem pair added in PR #8

nodes.summary: Operations take explicit context, return data; run/execute naming
nodes.detail: Every operation takes explicit KB/snapshot/workspace context and returns data, with no whole-environment AppEffects row. run… is reserved for effect interpretation and execute… for application execution that composes interpreters, while business logic stays in the effectful operation.

realised.evidence: run… interpreters from PR #7/#8; execute… command composition first appears with host/kyyn Composition in PR #44

nodes.summary: Application composition lives in Kyyn.Application.Compose, never 'Runner'
nodes.detail: Composition belongs in Kyyn.Application.Compose with optional Kyyn.Application.Execution.* modules; interpreter installers stay with their interpreter modules.

realised.evidence: Composition was built as Kyyn.Composition in host/kyyn (PR #44); no Kyyn.Application.Compose module exists at end of history, though the ADR still names it

nodes.summary: Plumbing FileSystem takes caller scope and relative path, no KB nouns
nodes.detail: The filesystem plumbing exposes operations over opaque DirectoryScope and RelativePath values and knows nothing of facts or evolutions; native failures become Failure rather than empty data. Atomic single-file replacement is not KB-level atomicity, which acceptance owns.

realised.evidence: FileSystem, DirectoryScope, ReadBytes, runFileSystemIO first appear in code in PR #8

nodes.summary: Guest file writes lower through writeRequestedFile with explicit base
nodes.detail: The host adapter for guest filesystem writes resolves path text against a composition-supplied base (the KB checkout for a file sink) into scoped FileSystem calls, needing no IOE in its row; it is location resolution, not a grant registry.

realised.evidence: writeRequestedFile never appears in code; file sinks remain unbuilt per seq 143 PR body

nodes.summary: FileSystem gains scoped temporary directories; plain writes not atomic
nodes.detail: WithTemporaryScope creates and always removes a private child of an explicitly supplied parent; WriteBytes populates private scopes without atomic-replacement promises, and paths are checked relative with no empty, . or .. components. ListEntries/WriteBytesAtomically are dropped from the initial API.

realised.evidence: PR #8 implements scoped FileSystem with temporary-directory cleanup for MicroHs compilation

nodes.summary: ReadTree captures a directory into an immutable FileTree
nodes.detail: ReadTree captures files under a scope with relative paths, rejecting symlinks, dropping empty dirs and mode bits, and failing on missing directories; it is sequential, not an atomic snapshot.

nodes.summary: CreateUniqueDirectory reserves a fresh random hex child exclusively
nodes.detail: Exclusive directory creation with random Word64 names, retrying only on collision and never reusing existing entries; allocation, not cryptographic identity.

realised.evidence: PR #32 implements exclusive allocation with concurrency tests

nodes.summary: ReplaceBytes atomic rename; ReadOptionalBytes distinguishes only missing paths
nodes.detail: ReplaceBytes writes a temp file in the destination directory and renames it over, so readers see old or new; ReadOptionalBytes returns Nothing only for missing paths, keeping unreadable data a Failure.

realised.evidence: PR #36 implements both with concurrency/cleanup tests

nodes.summary: ListDirectory enumerates immediate names; Nothing means absent
nodes.detail: Shallow sorted enumeration without reading contents; absent directory is Nothing, empty is Just [], other errors remain Failure.

realised.evidence: PR #39 adds ListDirectory for lifecycle enumeration

nodes.summary: Guest compilation and guest execution are distinct plumbing capabilities
nodes.detail: GuestCompilation only compiles and GuestExecution owns one-shot and conversational execution; callers running an existing artifact need only GuestExecution, and both interpreters lower through FileSystem and ProcessExecution without IOE.

realised.evidence: PR #102 commit 1cebb68 moves execution into GuestExecution; GuestCompilation only compiles

nodes.summary: Scoped locked-document persistence effect with current and archives
nodes.detail: DocumentPersistence exposes WithLockedDocument, a scoped local effect holding an exclusive lock across read/check/replace, with current state.dhall, archive operations and fresh stamps; it knows nothing of KBs or connectors.

realised.evidence: PR #102 commit 0663ec1 adds EvidenceStore over scoped DocumentPersistence

nodes.summary: Document persistence is latest-only; archive operations removed
nodes.detail: Following the latest-only evidence decision, DocumentAccess drops ArchiveCurrent/ClearArchives; only current bytes are retained under the scoped lock.

realised.evidence: PR #104: 'Scoped document persistence without archive operations'

nodes.summary: ClearCurrent removes the scope, reports existence; lock is a sibling
nodes.detail: Clearing deletes the scoped directory and returns whether it existed; the lock file sits beside the directory so clearing never changes lock identity, and replacement recreates the directory.

realised.evidence: PR #104: stable lock identity across clear; clear returns whether a cache existed

Desired-state reconciliation: removes status/date/basis, renames the table example to checkEvolution/executeCheckEvolution, and moves the runSchemaInspectionIO row to ADR 0005 (ownership move, not a change in requirement)

notes: Most of the lane is the FileSystem plumbing API growing one primitive per implementation PR (seqs 8-38), each written and built in the same step, so the spec tracked code tightly. The founding API itself was revised before any code: ListEntries/WriteBytesAtomically were dropped at seq 8 and atomic replacement only came back as ReplaceBytes at seq 35. Two founding commitments are still unrealised: Kyyn.Application.Compose (code uses Kyyn.Composition and the ADR was never corrected, even in the seq 143 reconciliation) and writeRequestedFile for guest/file-sink writes. The DocumentPersistence archive capability lived for a single step (83->84) before the latest-only evidence reversal removed it. I treated the five-layer list, package DAG and IOE confinement as one founding node, because they form one commitment.
